extracted.intended_audience: general readers, authors, publishers, librarians, and book‑industry professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Information and policies about how Kirkus Reviews selects, produces, and publishes book reviews (including the traditional unpaid review program and the paid Indie program), and the editorial standards that govern their reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional unpaid review program
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirkus Reviews has a traditional program of reviewing that does not require payment for reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books are reviewed under the traditional program without authors or publishers paying for the review; this represents the magazine's standard editorial review channel (as opposed to the paid Indie program).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indie program — paid reviews with editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirkus Reviews also offers an indie program that allows book authors to purchase, but not modify or influence, reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although authors may pay for an Indie review, they cannot change or influence the review content. Authors can choose whether or not to publish the review on the Kirkus website. Publication of Indie reviews in the print magazine or email newsletter is subject to Kirkus editor discretion (i.e., editorial selection decides which paid reviews appear more broadly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial discretion over publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirkus editors exercise discretion in deciding which Indie reviews get published in the magazine and in the email newsletter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being a paid Indie review does not guarantee placement in the magazine or newsletter; editorial judgment controls broader publication and selection for featured outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepublication previewing of titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirkus Reviews previews books before their publication and is published on the first and 15th of each month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kirkus receives advance copies/galley proofs to review titles prepublication; historically the service arranged to get galley proofs in advance and currently previews thousands of titles (over 10,000 per year), issuing reviews on a semi‑monthly schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial quality goals: readability, concision, accuracy, impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Under editorial changes (notably in 1985), the review format and style were modified for improved readability, concision, accuracy, and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kirkus's review style emphasizes clear, concise writing that accurately conveys assessment and aims to make an impact — these are expressed as the editorial standards guiding how reviews are written and edited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kirkus Prize categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirkus Reviews confers the annual Kirkus Prize to authors of fiction, nonfiction, and young readers' literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Kirkus Prize (established 2014) awards $50,000 annually across these three categories; eligibility is tied to those literary categories, though the page does not detail further judging criteria.
